questions.stem: An elderly patient with dementia is not compliant with oral medications. Which of the following will be beneficial in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rivastigmine
  • Rivastigmine can be prescribed in the form of a transdermal patch for management of dementia. Hence, leads to improved compliance to treatment.


Goodman & Gillman, 13th Edition, Chapter-18, Page No. 333-334.

questions.stem: A 75-year-old patient with CHF, chest x-ray shows batwing oedema & cardiac enlargement. Which of the following can help to reduce mortality & reduce further damage ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Carvedilol
  • Beta blockers are the group of drugs that improves mortality in patient of heart failure. Carvedilol is a beta + alpha blocker with anti – oxidant property & can prevent further ventricular dysfunction.
  • Carvedilol is a beta-blocker with alpha-blocking properties. It's known as a beta-blocker that also possesses antioxidant properties.
  • Carvedilol has been demonstrated to reduce mortality, improve symptoms, and slow the progression of heart failure.
  • It works by reducing the workload on the heart, improving cardiac function, and potentially preventing further damage to the heart muscle


Goodman & Gillman, 14th Edition, Chapter-33, Page No.646

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with ulcerative colitis presents with 2-3 episodes of bloody stools per day. What should be given to manage this patient:
questions.solutionHtml:
5 aminosalicylic acid
  • < 4 stools per day is a case of mild ulcerative colitis.
  • Also known as mesalamine, is often used as a first-line treatment for mild to moderate ulcerative colitis.
  • It works as an anti-inflammatory agent and can help reduce symptoms such as bloody stools, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.
  • In mild cases with few episodes of bloody stools per day, 5-aminosalicylic acid is often prescribed to induce and maintain remission.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 2482

questions.stem: What is the most useful drug to treat doxorubicin induced cardiotoxicity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexrazoxane
  • The quinone moieties of anthracyclines can form radical intermediates that react with O2 to produce superoxide anion radicals, which can generate H2 O2 and OH that attack DNA and oxidize DNA bases, leading to apoptosis.
  • Superoxide dismutase and catalase protect cells against this toxicity of the anthracyclines which can be augmented by exogenous antioxidants such as α-tocopherol or by the iron chelator dexrazoxane (protects against cardiotoxicity of anthracyclines)


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 70: Page No. 1368

questions.stem: A 12 year old boy presents with complaints of profuse watery stools and an elevated WBC count of 16000 cells/mm3. He has been on treatment with amoxicillin for the past 1 week. Which of the following is not used for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Albendazole
  • Metronidazole has been used as therapy for non severe C. difficile infection, although vancomycin or fidaxomicin are now preferred agents.
  • For patients with fulminant, life-threatening C. difficile infection, intravenous metronidazole is administered in combination with oral vancomycin.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 60: Page No. 1184

questions.stem: A young man is brought to the casualty with pinpoint pupils. Which of the following is the most likely substance he would have consumed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Opium
  • Among the given options, opioids are the only drugs that cause pinpoint pupils/miosis. Rest of the agents are known to cause dilatation of pupils/mydriasis.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 09: Page No. 162

questions.stem: Which of the following side effects of carbamazepine is more than ox-carbamazepine except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hyponatremia
  • Although most adverse effects are similar to those with carbamazepine, hyponatremia may occur more commonly with oxcarbazepine than with carbamazepine


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 20: Page No. 407

questions.stem: Which of the following mood stabilisers causes hepatotoxicity and hyperammonemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Valproate
  • Valproic acid has several effects on hepatic function like elevation of hepatic transaminases in plasma is observed in up to 40% of patients and often occurs asymptomatically during the first several months of therapy to fulminant hepatitis that is frequently fatal can occur.
  • Moreover, hyperammonemia is frequently associated with the use of valproic acid.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 20: Page No. 403

questions.stem: Which candida species is resistant to fluconazole?
questions.solutionHtml:
Candida krusei
  • Among the given options, strains of candida krusei are inherently resistant to fluconazole.
  • C. glabrata and C. krusei are considered intrinsically resistant to fluconazole, whereas 90% of C. auris isolates are resistant based on tentative breakpoints proposed by the CDC


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 61: Page No. 1198

questions.stem: Which of the following Drug is contraindicated in patient with history of hemophilia with HIV?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tipranavir
  • Tipranavir has an anti-coagulant effect. Hence, it is contraindicated in hemophiliacs as there is risk of increased bleeding.
  • This is an old question as this agent is very rarely used now a days.
  • Recent edition of standard textbooks has even removed the details of the drug

Toxicity of Tipranavir

  • Rare but potentially fatal hepatotoxicity
  • Rare but potentially fatal bleeding diathesis, including intracranial hemorrhage
  • Rarely used because of the availability of better-tolerated PIs


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 64: Page No. 1264

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs does not act via the ATP-binding cassette transporter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thiazide
  • Reason- Thiazide diuretics act by  SLC transporters operates passively without needing energy and translocates the substrate in the direction of its electrochemical gradient, i.e. from higher to lower concentration.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 04: Page No. 91

questions.stem: A 40 year old woman with multi drug resistant tuberculosis presents with fatigue, constipation, weight gain and neck swelling. On doing clinical investigation , it was found thyroid function profile is deranged suggestive of Hypothyroidism. Which of the following drugs is responsible for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ethionamide
  • The given history & thyroid function profile suggests that the patient has developed hypothyroidism while on anti-TB treatment.
  • Ethionamide is the second line anti tubercular drugs which has a risk of hypothyroidism.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 65: Page No.1276

questions.stem: A 25 year old male patient presents with several purpuric skin lesions and is diagnosed with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura. Which of the following tyrosine kinase inhibitors can be used in his condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fostamatinib
  • Bruton Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) Inhibitors: Bruton Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) protein plays important roles in the signal transduction and normal function of B cells as well as their malignant transformation.
  • B-cell receptor signaling recruits SYK followed by the activation of BTK and PI3Kδ, leading to further downstream responses and multiple cellular effects. Integrin signaling and chemokine receptor signaling can modulate the activity of the pathway.
  • Fostamatinib ( SYK kinase inhibitor): approved for the treatment of patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 71: Page No. 1394

questions.stem: Which of the following newly approved anti-diabetic drugs can be given for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and impaired renal function?
questions.solutionHtml:
Empagliflozin
  • Empagliflozin reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in patients with heart failure and a preserved ejection fraction, regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes (EMPEROR-Preserved trial)
  • Sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce the risk of hospitalization for heart failure in patients regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes (EMPEROR-reduced trial)


Goodman & Gilman 13th Edition, Page No. 879-880

questions.stem: Which of the given drugs is used for post herpetic neuralgia and spinal cord injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pregabalin
  • Pregabalin is a γ-aminobutyric acid analogues that inhibit neurotransmission.it is used in neuropathic pain syndromes.
  • Pregabalin is the drug of choice for neuropathic pains like – post herpetic neuralgia, diabetic neuropathy, spinal cord injury etc


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 22: Page No. 440

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs are not used in the management of a thyrotoxic crisis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aspirin
  • Aspirin is not used in case of thyroid storm. As it causes decreased protein binding & increased levels of free T3, T4.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 47: Page No. 592

questions.stem: A patient on fluoxetine presented with palpitations. ECG showed QTc prolongation. Which of the following drugs can cause this ECG feature?
questions.solutionHtml:
Methadone
  • Methadone is an opioid with potential risk of causing QTc prolongation.


Goodman & Gilman 14th Edition, Chapter 23: Page No. 461

questions.stem: Which of the following anti-microbial acts on 50S subunit of ribosome?
questions.solutionHtml:
Linezolid
  • linezolid is the antibiotic that binds to the 50S subunit of ribosome & inhibits protein synthesis.
  • Aztreonam binds to penicillin binding protein-3 & inhibits cell wall synthesis
  • Rifampicin – inhibits the bacterial DNA dependent RNA polymerase
  • Daptomycin causes disruption of the bacterial cell membrane.


KD Tripathi Essentials of Medical pharmacology 8th Edition, Page No. 807

questions.stemHtml: What is the site of action of valproate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Drug VI
  • Valproate is an inhibitor of GABA metabolism.



KDT, 8TH EDITION, PAGE NO 444-445
